summary: @servicetitan/admin-sql-table preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated in-tarball payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs", which runs automatically on npm install. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip into a temp directory, extracts it, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. If a local bun is already available it is used directly. math_init.js is a ~720 KB single-line file matching the classic string-array obfuscator shape (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, rotator function `WV8StW` that shuffles a large numeric/character array `n7gIxM`, randomized identifiers such as MmgoCP, etDiOOB, hc1jfK9). None of the readable strings correspond to the advertised React SQL-table component purpose. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope and declares peer dependencies on other @servicetitan/* packages, borrowing that scope's trust while shipping install-time execution of opaque code under a freshly fetched second-language runtime that bypasses Node-only inspection. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern combined with a bundled obfuscated payload, a scope-squat name, and lack of any legitimate reason for a React UI package to require Bun at install time indicate a supply-chain attack against installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
